subtopic: Euler Form, De Moivre's Theorem & Roots of a Complex Number
title: Roots live on a circle, equally spaced

board_content.text: Taking an nth root divides the angle
An $n$th root divides the angle by $n$ — but the angle is known only up to $2\pi$.
So there are $n$ legitimate answers, spaced $\tfrac{2\pi}{n}$ apart.

board_content.caption: n roots = vertices of a regular n-gon

board_content.text: They lie on a circle of radius $r^{1/n}$, forming a regular $n$-gon.
Powers multiply the angle; roots divide it over n branches.
The $n$th roots of unity are that polygon inscribed in the unit circle, one vertex at $1$.

segments_english.text: Euler form makes powers trivial, and it makes roots beautifully geometric. Here is the key picture.
Taking an nth root divides the angle by n. But remember the argument was only ever known up to a full turn, two pi.
That extra freedom is exactly why there are n legitimate answers, not one. They come out equally spaced, two pi over n apart, as you fold in each extra turn.
So the n roots are the vertices of a regular n-gon. The cube roots form an equilateral triangle; the fourth roots form a square.
They all sit on a circle whose radius is the nth root of the original modulus, spread evenly around it.
Contrast this with powers. In Euler form, z to the n is r to the n times e to the i n theta: a single answer, with the angle multiplied by n.
So keep the duality straight: powers multiply the angle and give one number, while roots divide the angle but spread over n branches.
And the special case we keep meeting, the nth roots of unity, is simply that regular polygon inscribed in the unit circle, with one vertex pinned at one.

segments_hinglish.text: Euler form powers ko trivial banata hai, aur roots ko khoobsurati se geometric. Ye rahi key picture.
Ek nth root angle ko n se divide karta hai. Par yaad rakho argument sirf ek full turn, two pi, tak hi known tha.
Wahi extra freedom exactly kyun hai ki n legitimate answers hote hain, ek nahi. Wo equally spaced nikalte hain, two pi over n apart, jaise aap har extra turn fold karte ho.
To n roots ek regular n-gon ke vertices hain. Cube roots ek equilateral triangle banate hain; fourth roots ek square.
Wo sab ek circle par baithte hain jiska radius original modulus ka nth root hai, uske around evenly faile hue.
Ise powers se contrast karo. Euler form mein, z to the n hai r to the n times e to the i n theta: ek single answer, angle n se multiply hua.
To duality clear rakho: powers angle ko multiply karke ek number dete hain, jabki roots angle ko divide karte hain par n branches par faile hote hain.
Aur wo special case jo baar baar milta hai, nth roots of unity, bas wahi regular polygon hai unit circle mein inscribed, ek vertex one par pinned.
